rv.q: As a dramatic simulacrum of the past two decades of western politics, David Edgar's play explores some pressing questions where the real-world stakes could not be higher. It's unfortunate that these stakes are rarely matched by the dramatic ones.
The play is beautifully plotted, full of betrayals, reversals, blind spots and unintended outcomes, with the consequences of human flaws playing out on the widest scale imaginable.
The writing is vigorous, the situations taut in this loftily ambitious work.

cn.t: David Edgar's intelligent political drama earns praise for its sharp topicality and gripping examination of electoral strategy, with critics highlighting its beautiful craft and timely exploration of post-truth politics.
